<link> View a sample streamlined timetable </link>
Standard timetable
Our standard timetable allows you to choose your class times across the workweek. Online (domestic students only) and on-campus classes run between 9am and 5pm on weekdays (Melbourne time). The standard timetable gives you more flexibility to spread your classes over the week and more flexibility in your elective unit selection.
Most on-campus units run as 1 x 2-hour lecture and 1 x 2-hour tutorial each week.

Choosing your timetable
We know that scheduling your classes around your work, family and social commitments can be tricky.
Classes in our standard timetable are offered across various weekdays at various times. You can pick and choose which classes suits you.
Classes in our streamlined timetable are condensed into two weekdays and the timetable is fixed for your whole diploma program.
The standard and streamlined timetables offer the same number of class hours per week, it’s just a matter of choosing which model suits your lifestyle best.

Business
Commerce
Information Technology

Student Learning Advisors
Ensure a smooth transition to university-level studies
Student Learning Advisors are professional staff who provide learning support across all Deakin campuses.
You can book half-hour individual or group appointments (either on-campus or online) with a Student Learning Advisor for help in the following key areas:
time management and organisation
study skills
research skills and using the library
paraphrasing, summarising, and quoting
referencing

exam preparation
guidance on improving English language skills
guidance on academic integrity, collusion, and contract cheating.

Student Mentors
Learn from your high-achieving peers
Book with a mentor to chat about your studies, life in Australia, seeking extra support or getting involved in the Deakin College community.

settling into life at college and getting involved
success at Deakin College by talking about the expectations of your lecturers and how to manage your time effectively
getting organised and forming effective study habits to last throughout your university studies
valuable study tips and the tools to help you succeed in your units

proof-read or edit work for students
re-teach the content of classes/tutorials
assist students with the content of assignments, as this would be collusion

Australian/Permanent residents can study part-time. International students must study full-time to meet visa conditions.

Failure to dispute an incorrect Commonwealth Assistance Notice results in this fee liability being reported to the Australian Taxation Office (ATO).
Commonwealth Higher Education Student Support Number (CHESSN)
The CAN notice will provide students with their Commonwealth Higher Education Student Support Number (CHESSN). Students CHESSN is unique and will enable them to access information on their FEE-HELP balance via the <link> myGov website </link>.
How do you withdraw your enrolment in unit(s) of study?
To withdraw from a unit(s) of study a students may make changes to their original enrolment/unit selection on-line through the <link> Deakin College student portal </link>. After on-line enrolment is closed, students who want to make an enrolment change will be required to complete the appropriate ‘Enrolment Variation’ form and submit to Deakin College reception on or before the census date.
What happens if you withdraw on or before the census date?

Please note:  This form is not to be used to withdraw from all/remaining units - please use Leave of Absence or Withdrawal Form otherwise this could delay your application.

This form is used to add or remove a unit(s) from your enrolment if you are not able to do this yourself on the student portal (up to week 2).
Students can self enrol up to end of week 2 - only send a form if there is a clash with classes or other enrolling issues.
Students cannot add units after week 2 - only cancel/withdraw units.
Friday 14th November - Census Date - last day to cancel a unit without Financial Penalty
Friday 12th December - last day to withdraw from a unit without Academic Penalty 
Students cannot withdraw from units after week 10.

Important Information Before you complete this form, please read:  During the enrolment period (until the end of week two), students may make changes to their enrolment via the Student Portal, provided that vacancies are available in classes.   Complete this Enrolment Variation form to withdraw from a unit after the Student Portal enrolment period closes or if you have issue(s) enrolling via the Student Portal. A new unit(s) enrolment cannot be added after the Student Portal enrolment period closes.   Students are required to continue to attend classes for which they were originally enrolled until they are notified by Deakin College through the Student Portal of the outcome of their Enrolment Variation request (check your Deakin College email address).   Changing from one class to another class in the same unit is not permitted via this form, please try to make this change yourself in the Student Portal before the end of week two.   Student visa conditions require international students to maintain a full-time study load (3 or 4 units) unless they are in the last trimester of study at Deakin College. Note: international students are required to complete their course within the course duration as specified in their confirmation of enrolment (COE).   Domestic students will not incur a fee penalty up to the end of week four (4) of the trimester (census date) if they withdraw from a unit. International students will incur a fee penalty up to the end of week four (4) (census date) if they withdraw from a unit.   Students can withdraw from a unit after week four, however, a ‘W’ (Withdrawn) grade will be recorded against the unit and fees will be forfeited.   Units withdrawn after week eight (8) of a trimester will receive a Withdrawn Fail (WN) grade. This means that you have withdrawn and deemed to have failed. This fail grade will be included in the calculation of your Weighted Average Mark (WAM) and may affect your transfer to Deakin University. Please check your WAM through the Student Portal > Student HUB > Understanding Your WAM. Students cannot withdraw from units after week ten. Refer to the <link> Enrolment, Fees and Charges Policy </link> for further information.   STUDENT DETAILS:

A Change of Course Application must be submitted prior to the start of the next study period. It will only be processed after the official release of academic results.
A Change of course application should not be submitted after Friday of study Week 1.

This form is also for changing from Burwood Campus to Geelong Campus or Geelong to Burwood Campus.

Important Information  Before you complete this form, please read: Applications must be submitted prior to the start of a trimester. Applications will only be processed, for currently enrolled students, after the release of results. Students who have been placed on a conditional enrolment in any trimester will be required to undertake an interview with the Academic Coordinator before this application is approved. Students who receive a ‘show cause’ condition for failure to achieve satisfactory course progress will not be eligible to apply for a change of course. Students must have no outstanding fees. Yes, depending on what you wish to change, there are several options available according to the guidelines:

### 1. Changing Units (Enrolment Variation)
* **Adding or swapping units:** You can make changes to your enrolment/unit selection online through the [Deakin College student portal](https://axis.navitas.com/) up until the end of Week 2, provided vacancies are available. You cannot add units after Week 2.
* **Changing classes within the same unit:** Must be done by yourself in the Student Portal before the end of Week 2 (this cannot be requested via the Enrolment Variation form).
* **Withdrawing from units:** If the Student Portal enrolment period has closed, you must submit an Enrolment Variation form. 
  * International students incur a fee penalty if withdrawing up to the end of Week 4 (census date).
  * Withdrawing after Week 4 results in a ‘W’ (Withdrawn) grade and forfeited fees.
  * Withdrawing after Week 8 results in a ‘WN’ (Withdrawn Fail) grade, which impacts your WAM.
  * You cannot withdraw from units after Week 10.
* **Study load requirement:** As an international student, your visa conditions require you to maintain a full-time study load (3 or 4 units) unless you are in your final trimester, and complete your course within the duration specified on your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).

### 2. Changing Course or Campus
* You can apply to change your course or transfer between the Burwood Campus and Geelong Campus.
* **Deadlines:** Applications must be submitted prior to the start of the trimester (and should not be submitted after Friday of study Week 1). They are only processed after the official release of academic results.
* **Requirements:** You must have no outstanding fees. If you are under 18, you must provide a supporting letter from a parent/legal guardian from your home country. Sponsored students must seek approval from their sponsor. Students with a 'show cause' condition are not eligible.

### 3. Study Mode (Online vs. On-Campus)
* International students are not permitted to study online and must study on campus.

Your resume (or CV)
Your resume, or CV, should outline your experience, skills and qualifications. You should adjust your resume for each job application to highlight the most relevant experience. It’s important to keep your resume clear, concise and easy to read.
A resume should at least include:
Your contact details
A profile, objective or summary with an overview of your skills, achievements and goals
Your experience, including companies you have worked for, your job title and the specific duties of your position
Your education, including the names of the educational institutions and any qualifications
Your skills, keeping them specific to the job you’re applying for

Some roles in Australia may require additional legal checks or specialised health and safety training. These are generally fairly easy to access with many providers offering what’s required. Some common checks and training are:

Mindfulness & meditation
Learning to live in the moment
Mindfulness is about learning to train your attention to the present moment without dwelling on what has happened in the past or worrying about the future.
The basic practice – or ‘meditation’ – can be developed over time with practice and involves intentionally placing your attention on the breath and observing each rise and fall. It is natural that your mind will wander, but part of the practice is being aware of when this happens and being able to gently redirect your mind to the present and back to the breath.
Benefits of mindfulness:
Reduce stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms
Increase resilience and peace of mind
Enhance cognitive performance eg. concentration, memory and processing speed
Improve study and work performance
Improve relationships and overall wellbeing
